item.title: Roadmap
item.description:
Roadmap

Current status (2026-09-28)

Requirements baseline v3.2 frozen; materials for 23 capability domains dispatched to 23 capability-center repos (18 existing + 5 new); tech-base opic-techbase in place; website first release.

Modeling phase (next)

Entry requirements: domain_rules.py (hard block for zero-approval domains), technical primary key, domain.object string carrier, three-variant adapter layer, reverse interface inventory, 30-location count reconciled with full manifest, unilateral declaration whitelist, protocol-commitment ↔ semantic-carrier reconciliation; four execution disciplines.

item.title: Ontology Engineering Method
item.description:
Ontology Engineering Method (core differentiator)

The fundamental difference from “requirements doc + development”: requirements are a computable, verifiable, freezable semantic system.

Nine cross-cutting criteria

① explicit source of truth ② write-path convergence ③ credential lineage across eight positions ④ append-only ledger ⑤ approval-decision families (irreversible-failure / boundary-expansion; no approval without an alternative mechanism) ⑥ five execution paradigms ⑦ no-side-effect execution family ⑧ recompute-cost criterion ⑨ enforcement at the consumer side.

item.title: Architecture
item.description:
Overall Architecture

Three layers

Layer Content Key constraint
Layer 1 · Users platform operator / tenants / developers / end users one shared identity & authorization semantics
Layer 2 · Platform ontology-driven intelligent computing capabilities 23 domains, machine-verifiable
Layer 3 · AI applications dependency-isolated engines & MaaS consumption fully swappable without requirement churn

Detail mirrors the Chinese page; this entry keeps the architecture summary.

item.title: Platform Intro
item.description:
OPIC Open Intelligent Computing Platform

OPIC is an ontology-driven intelligent computing + MaaS platform: 23 capability domains form a complete semantic layer, covering the full path from physical compute onboarding to AI application consumption.

Three differentiators

  1. Ontology-driven requirements engineering — requirements are a machine-verifiable semantic system: one Requirements Specification plus one Editorial Note per domain, gated by 927 automated checks, a consistency scan (130 cross-domain references, zero dangling links), and 13 self-checks in Chapter 9; the baseline is frozen by a SHA-256 manifest.
  2. Layer 3 is fully swappable — all open-source dependencies are isolated in the dependency layer; swapping an engine does not trigger requirement changes except when the swap exposes a semantic gap.
  3. All 20 industry-benchmark must-haves met (2026-09 refresh: batch inference, structured output, guardrail as independent API, split caching billing, model retirement commitments, etc.).

Snapshot (requirements baseline v3.2)

Metric Value
Capability domains 23
Spec / editorial lines 47,628 / 9,421
Machine checks 927 · FAIL 0 / WARN 0
Cross-domain refs 130 · broken 0
Four review rounds 88 findings · 86 closed / 2 tracked
